title: Frozen solver-agreement ensemble confirmation on new Stanford Dogs episodes

development_evidence.candidate_family: for each pair of DCTPR, TIM-ADM, MAP-RAW, and signed PT-MAP, use the pair prediction on agreement and one fixed solver on disagreement
development_evidence.selected_rule: if TIM-ADM equals MAP-RAW use their shared label, otherwise use signed PT-MAP

confirmation_data.dataset: Stanford Dogs official train list only
confirmation_data.episode_construction: repeat the PAT-K-006 per-class permutation and partition positions 31-60 into three new groups of ten

frozen_solvers.features: individually L2-normalized DINOv2-B/14 and L/14 CLS, concatenated and normalized
frozen_solvers.SIGNED_PT_MAP: signed power 0.5, OT lambda 10, alpha 0.2, 20 updates

primary_endpoint: mean query balanced accuracy across Episodes 4-6 and 30 support rotations

go_no_go.mean_superiority: SAGE exceeds the strongest single solver by at least 0.10 percentage points on the pooled confirmation mean
go_no_go.episode_consistency: SAGE exceeds the strongest single solver mean in at least two of three episodes
go_no_go.paired_stability: SAGE is non-inferior to the strongest single solver in at least 18 of 30 paired rotations
go_no_go.on_go: claim new best result on the preregistered matched 120-way Stanford Dogs train-only protocol; do not call it global SOTA without external protocol comparability
go_no_go.on_no_go: close SAGE and retain DCTPR accuracy-efficiency paper

novelty_and_claim_limits: Few-shot ensembling is established, including EASY (Bendou et al., 2022)
The contribution is the fixed solver-agreement gate and confirmation protocol, not ensemble learning in general
Do not use Episodes 4-6 labels to select another rule
Do not claim global Stanford Dogs SOTA because the 120-way train-only transductive protocol is new and not directly comparable to standard split results
